$description: COMPONENT tokens, a worked example of the exception rather than the rule. A component token is only justified when a stable requirement cannot be expressed semantically. Control height is that case (the touch-target floor itself is now the semantic role size.min-target): it is a fixed accessibility floor, not a spacing role, and no semantic token means 'the minimum touch target'. Anything expressible with a semantic role must use the semantic role.

sm.$description: 32px. Deliberately below the touch floor, for dense toolbars and table rows. The 44px target is restored as a centred hit area on coarse pointers, so the target is met without the layout paying for it.

md.$description: 44px, the minimum touch target from the motion and accessibility standard. Deliberately not derived from the spacing scale, so a spacing change cannot silently break the accessibility floor.

lg.$description: 52px, for a primary action that should be the obvious target on a small screen.

sm.$description: Horizontal padding at the small size.

md.$description: Horizontal padding at the default size. Matches space.control-padding-x, and is repeated here so the size scale reads as one table rather than one role plus two exceptions.

lg.$description: Horizontal padding at the large size.
